name: Eiffel Tower
fact: Built for the 1889 World's Fair, it was the tallest structure on Earth for 41 years.

name: Statue of Liberty
fact: A gift from France, dedicated in 1886 and standing on Liberty Island.

name: Colosseum
fact: The largest amphitheatre ever built, once holding more than 50,000 spectators.

name: Great Wall
fact: Its branches and sections stretch more than 21,000 kilometres across northern China.

name: Taj Mahal
fact: A white marble mausoleum completed in 1653 for Mumtaz Mahal.

name: Machu Picchu
fact: A 15th-century Inca citadel sitting about 2,430 metres above sea level.

name: Christ the Redeemer
fact: The 30-metre art deco statue overlooks Rio from Corcovado mountain.

name: Pyramids of Giza
fact: The Great Pyramid is the only surviving wonder of the ancient world.

name: Sydney Opera House
fact: Its shell roof was designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon and opened in 1973.

name: Big Ben
fact: Big Ben is properly the bell inside the Elizabeth Tower at the Palace of Westminster.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
fact: Its distinctive colour is officially called International Orange.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
fact: The tower began tilting during construction because of soft ground on one side.

name: Petra
fact: The Nabataean city was carved directly into rose-coloured sandstone cliffs.

name: Stonehenge
fact: The prehistoric stone circle was raised in stages between 3000 and 2000 BC.

name: Acropolis of Athens
fact: The Parthenon on the Acropolis was completed in 432 BC.

name: Sagrada Família
fact: Antoni Gaudí's basilica has been under construction since 1882.

name: Angkor Wat
fact: The largest religious monument in the world, covering over 160 hectares.

name: Mount Fuji
fact: Japan's highest peak at 3,776 metres, and an active stratovolcano.

name: Burj Khalifa
fact: At 828 metres it has been the world's tallest building since 2010.

name: Chichén Itzá
fact: The El Castillo pyramid has 365 steps, one for each day of the year.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
fact: The 19th-century palace inspired the classic fairy-tale castle silhouette.

name: Brandenburg Gate
fact: Completed in 1791, it became a symbol of Germany's division and reunification.

name: Red Square
fact: Saint Basil's Cathedral on the square was finished in 1561.

name: Hagia Sophia
fact: Built as a cathedral in 537, it later served as a mosque and a museum.

name: Table Mountain
fact: Its famous flat top is often covered by a cloud known as the tablecloth.

name: Victoria Falls
fact: The waterfall on the Zambezi forms the largest sheet of falling water on Earth.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
fact: Africa's highest point at 5,895 metres and the world's tallest free-standing mountain.

name: Serengeti National Park
fact: Home to the annual migration of more than a million wildebeest.

name: Great Barrier Reef
fact: The world's largest coral reef system, visible from space.

name: Uluru
fact: The sandstone monolith is sacred to the Anangu people of Central Australia.

name: Milford Sound
fact: A fiord carved by glaciers, with cliffs rising over 1,200 metres from the water.

name: Grand Canyon
fact: The Colorado River carved the canyon over roughly six million years.

name: Niagara Falls
fact: More than 3,000 tonnes of water flow over the falls every second.

name: CN Tower
fact: The 553-metre tower held the record for tallest free-standing structure for 32 years.

name: Panama Canal
fact: The 82-kilometre canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

name: Salar de Uyuni
fact: The world's largest salt flat becomes a giant mirror in the rainy season.

name: Iguazu Falls
fact: The system has 275 separate drops along the Argentina–Brazil border.

name: Easter Island Moai
fact: Nearly 900 monolithic statues were carved by the Rapa Nui people.

name: Galápagos Islands
fact: Charles Darwin's 1835 visit shaped his theory of evolution by natural selection.

name: Forbidden City
fact: The palace complex has 980 surviving buildings and served 24 emperors.

name: Terracotta Army
fact: Around 8,000 clay soldiers were buried with China's first emperor.

name: Mount Everest
fact: At 8,849 metres it is the highest point above sea level on Earth.

name: Petronas Towers
fact: The twin towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.

name: Marina Bay Sands
fact: Its rooftop SkyPark spans three towers and holds a 150-metre infinity pool.

name: Borobudur
fact: The 9th-century Buddhist temple is the largest of its kind in the world.

name: Blue Mosque
fact: Named for the tens of thousands of blue İznik tiles lining its interior.

name: Dead Sea
fact: Its shore is the lowest land elevation on Earth, about 430 metres below sea level.

name: Atomium
fact: Built for Expo 58, it models an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

name: Little Mermaid
fact: The bronze statue from 1913 is only 1.25 metres tall.

name: Blue Lagoon
fact: The geothermal spa is fed by water from a nearby power station.

name: Charles Bridge
fact: Construction of the Gothic bridge began in 1357 under Charles IV.

name: Kremlin
fact: The fortified complex has walls stretching more than two kilometres.

name: Alhambra
fact: The Moorish palace and fortress dates mainly from the 13th and 14th centuries.

name: Windmills of Kinderdijk
fact: Nineteen 18th-century windmills once drained the surrounding polders.

name: Matterhorn
fact: The near-symmetrical 4,478-metre peak straddles the Swiss–Italian border.

name: Marrakech Medina
fact: The walled old city dates from the 11th century and centres on Jemaa el-Fnaa.

name: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela
fact: Eleven medieval churches were cut downward into solid volcanic rock.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
fact: The largest mud-brick building in the world, replastered by the town each year.

name: Okavango Delta
fact: A rare inland river delta that empties into the Kalahari rather than the sea.
